drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Subject to our client’s approval and agreement on complete documentation, we have revised the draft to reflect your proposed $450,000 base salary, 50% target bonus, and 18 months of salary and benefits continuation. The revisions clarify bonus eligibility, define good reason, and condition severance on an effective release. We have also replaced the post-employment non-compete with confidentiality protections that preserve lawful reporting and the Executive’s ability to use general skills and experience. Please confirm whether these terms provide a basis for finalizing the documentation.

edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. The Executive’s annual base salary shall be $450,000, payable in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll practices. The Executive shall be eligible for an annual bonus with a target equal to 50% of annual base salary, with actual payment determined by achievement of performance objectives established by the Board or its compensation committee after consultation with the Executive and subject to the applicable bonus plan. The Executive shall be eligible to participate in employee benefit plans made available to similarly situated senior executives, subject to their terms.

3. SEVERANCE. If the Company terminates the Executive’s employment without Cause or the Executive resigns for Good Reason, the Company shall provide continued payment of base salary at the rate in effect immediately before termination, without giving effect to any reduction constituting Good Reason, for 18 months, and continued medical, dental and vision coverage for the Executive and eligible dependents on the same cost-sharing basis as immediately before termination for up to 18 months. If continued participation is unavailable, the Company shall provide an economically equivalent benefit, subject to applicable law. Benefits continuation shall end when the Executive becomes eligible for comparable coverage through another employer. Severance is conditioned on the Executive executing and not revoking a customary release of claims within 60 days after termination and complying with continuing confidentiality obligations. Accrued salary, vested benefits and properly reimbursable business expenses shall be paid regardless of whether a release is executed. Good Reason means, without the Executive’s written consent, a material reduction in base salary, a material diminution in duties or authority, a required relocation of the principal work location by more than 50 miles, or a material breach of this Agreement by the Company. The Executive must give written notice within 90 days after the condition first arises, allow 30 days to cure, and resign within 30 days after the cure period expires if the condition remains uncured. Cause, severance payment timing and any provisions necessary for compliance with Section 409A shall be addressed in the definitive documentation.

4. CONFIDENTIALITY. No post-employment non-compete shall apply. During and after employment, the Executive shall not use or disclose the Company’s confidential business information except in performing duties for the Company or as authorized by the Company. Confidential information excludes information that becomes publicly available without breach, is lawfully received from a third party without a duty of confidentiality, or is independently developed without use of confidential information. These restrictions do not prevent use of general skills and experience, disclosures required by law, communications with governmental authorities, protected whistleblowing or other legally protected activity. No prior authorization or notice to the Company is required for protected reporting. Upon termination, the Executive shall return Company property and confidential information, subject to customary exceptions for personal employment records and legally required retention. Definitive documentation shall include applicable statutory trade-secret immunity notices.

receiver.message_back: The revised economics and removal of the non-compete provide a basis for finalizing, subject to our client’s approval and agreement on complete documentation, including objective bonus criteria established promptly and not retroactively changed, a narrowly defined Cause standard with notice and cure where appropriate, and definite, Section 409A-compliant severance payment dates. The release must not impose new restrictive covenants, and any forfeiture for breach of confidentiality should require a material breach established by final adjudication, with notice and an opportunity to cure where curable.
